transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess they brought me in because of what’s been happening at the warehouse. I’ll just kind of freeze with my arms up near the forklift, or I start copying the beeping sounds and the hand signals. Sometimes I move boxes into these little patterns, even when everyone’s yelling at me to stop.
Have you had trouble understanding or connecting with other people since you were a child?
I don’t really know. I mean, I had friends sometimes, and school was mostly normal, I think. I don’t remember having a big problem understanding people when I was a kid.
When you freeze like that, are you aware of what’s happening around you?

Kind of, yeah. I know people are around, and I can hear them yelling sometimes, but I just get stuck doing it. Like I’ll be standing there with my arms up by the forklift, or copying the beeps and signals, and even if I know it’s weird, I don’t really stop right away.
When this starts happening, does it feel like your body is moving on its own, out of your control?

Yeah… it kind of does. Like I know I’m there, but my body just starts doing it — holding my arms up, copying the forklift beeps or the hand signals, moving the boxes into those weird patterns. I can hear people telling me to stop, but I don’t stop right away.
Have you been diagnosed with any brain or nervous system illness?
No, not that I know of. I haven’t been told I have anything like that.
Have you been hearing voices when no one is there?
I don’t think so. I mean, I hear people around me sometimes, but I haven’t noticed voices when nobody’s there.
Do these episodes tend to start when you’re under a lot of stress?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed it being tied to stress exactly. Sometimes it just starts happening, and I don’t always know why.
Do you believe that someone or something is controlling your movements?
I don’t really know. I haven’t noticed my movements being controlled by someone else. It feels like I’m the one moving, as far as I can tell.
Outside of these episodes, have you been much less emotional or less interested in people or activities than you used to be?
I’m not sure. I mean, I don’t think I’ve noticed a big change like that. Some days I keep to myself, but I can’t really say if I’m less emotional or less interested than before.
Have you been feeling that people are trying to harm you or plot against you?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve noticed people plotting against me or trying to hurt me, not in a clear way. I just… haven’t really thought about it like that.
Do your thoughts ever feel jumbled up or hard to make sense of?

Yeah. Sometimes when I’m talking, it comes out all mixed up. Like at work, my supervisor asks which pallets are supposed to go on the truck, and I’ll start explaining from the load sheet, but then I’m talking about my old house, then fishing, then church boxes or something. By the time I’m done, nobody knows what I was trying to say.
Have you had a strong feeling that ordinary things around you carry a special message meant just for you?
I don’t think so. I mean, I notice stuff around me like anyone would, but I haven’t really felt like it was some special message just for me.
Before these episodes began, did you have any recent seizure, head injury, or serious illness?
I’m not sure. I don’t remember having a seizure or hitting my head bad or anything like that. I don’t think I was seriously sick right before it started.
Have you felt that outside forces are controlling your actions or putting thoughts into your mind?
I don’t think so. I haven’t really felt like something outside me is moving me around or putting thoughts in my head. My thoughts can get confusing, but they feel like they’re still mine.
Have you been speaking much less than usual lately?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve been talking that much, but I haven’t been paying close attention to it.
Have you felt that your thoughts were being broadcast so that other people could know them?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed my thoughts being broadcast like that, or that people can hear them.
When someone touches you or firmly guides you during one of these episodes, do you stop what you’re doing?

Sometimes, yeah. If somebody actually grabs my arm or moves me, I might stop for a second. But at the warehouse I’ve been doing stuff like just freezing there with my arms up by the forklift, or copying the beeping sounds and hand signals, or moving boxes into weird little patterns even when people are yelling at me to stop.
During these episodes, when someone tries to gently move your arm into a different position, does it stay where they put it?

I don’t really know about my arm staying where they put it. What I do know is they brought me in because at the warehouse I’ve been freezing with my arms up by the forklift, copying the beeping sounds and hand signals, and moving boxes into weird patterns even when people are yelling at me to stop.
During these episodes, when someone tries to move you, do you actively resist them?

I don’t know if I’m resisting exactly. I guess what they notice is I’ll get stuck doing things at the warehouse, like standing there with my arms up by the forklift, or copying the beeping and hand signals, or putting boxes into these strange little patterns even when people are yelling at me to stop.
Have these freezing and copying episodes, along with your mixed-up speech, been happening for at least a month?
Yeah… it’s definitely been more than a month. The mixed-up talking and the weird stuff at work have been going on for about six months now.

final_diagnosis.reason: The presentation is most consistent with catatonic schizophrenia: persistent psychotic disorganization with prominent catatonic behaviors for about six months, including stupor/posturing-like freezing, echophenomena, stereotyped/purposeless behavior, and disorganized speech. Neurologic illness, recent seizure/head injury, and clear substance/medical explanations were not supported in the interview. Although classic positive symptoms like delusions or hallucinations were not clearly endorsed, schizophrenia can be diagnosed when marked catatonic symptoms occur together with characteristic thought disorganization and sustained functional disturbance.
